title: How AI is changing software engineering at Shopify with Farhan Thawar
summary: Shopify's head of engineering describes company-wide AI adoption: unlimited token spend, MCP everywhere, AI in interviews, and many AI-fluent interns.

assertions.quote: the growth in cursor at Shopify is happening a lot outside of engineering and outside of R&D finance sales support

verdicts.note: Tools like Lovable, v0, Replit let non-developers produce working prototypes; widely observed.

assertions.quote: yes you can submit a PR but you have to understand the code you are writing yourself before exactly before you submit it

verdicts.note: Ownership and maintainability require understanding; it's a reasonable review standard rather than an empirical finding.

assertions.quote: you might generate 10,000 lines of code for a very simple uh application feature that now the burden on engineering to read

verdicts.note: The SmartBear/Cisco review study found defect detection drops beyond ~200-400 LOC per session; AI makes large PRs cheap to produce.

assertions.quote: if you're building infrastructure for the internet you likely want to understand how that's being built

verdicts.note: Unreviewed AI-built apps commonly ship with security, scaling and maintainability problems; prototypes are their sweet spot.

assertions.quote: I still believe this is Jevan's paradox. The more we get, the more we want.

verdicts.note: Jevons effects are historically common and plausible for software, but whether demand growth outpaces productivity for developer headcount is unproven.

assertions.quote: the AI agents are going to help the best engineers more than the mediocre engineer

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.

assertions.quote: I convinced Toby to hire a thousand interns this term

verdicts.note: IBM, LinkedIn, Cloudflare and others publicly announced more junior hiring in 2026, citing pipeline and AI fluency; still a minority of employers.

assertions.quote: We have a leaderboard where we um actively celebrate the people who use the most tokens.

verdicts.note: Goodhart's law applies: Orosz reports leaderboards and spend targets at large firms prompting busywork; consistent with past experience of line-of-code metrics.

assertions.quote: your impact is going to be evaluated as if you had the tool

verdicts.note: Reports of token-maxing and resentment support it, but some mandated rollouts (e.g. Shopify, Coinbase) report adoption gains; evidence is anecdotal either way.

assertions.quote: If they don't use a co-pilot, they usually get creamed by someone who does.

verdicts.note: Some companies allow AI or changed formats (e.g. Meta AI-enabled rounds), but LeetCode-style screens remain common.

assertions.quote: $1,000 a month is too cheap. Like it's too like if I can get 10 percent more, it is way too cheap.

verdicts.note: The arithmetic holds if gains are real, but measured gains are modest and uneven (Stanford, METR, DORA), and the speaker admits they can't measure them.
Airbnb says total cost (LLM API plus 6 weeks of engineering) was far below the manual estimate, even with high retry counts, but gives no dollar figures and covers only one migration.

assertions.quote: tech debt reduction, refactoring, u making things easier to read, like those are the things I'm seeing the best engineers at Shopify use AI tooling

verdicts.note: Airbnb and Google migration case studies show large mechanical refactors sped up a lot with AI, though results need careful review and broad cleanup claims are mostly anecdotal.
